step_down.name: Step Release

double_peak.name: Double Peak

half_quick.name: Quick Half Squeeze

half_hold.name: Half Long Hold
half_hold.desc: Squeeze half way and hold it there for a long time; then let go fully.

wave.name: Wave
wave.desc: Squeeze fully, let go half way, squeeze fully again, then drop to half and hold it long. Let go fully at the end.

what.title: What is the pelvic floor muscle?
body: A group of muscles stretched like a hammock across the bottom of your pelvis.
It holds up the bladder and bowel, supports urinary control and sexual function, and strengthens penis control.
Like any muscle, it gets stronger when trained regularly and correctly.
body_female: A group of muscles stretched like a hammock across the bottom of your pelvis.
It holds up the bladder and bowel and supports urinary control and sexual function.
Like any muscle, it gets stronger when trained regularly and correctly.
what.artAlt: The pelvis with the pelvic floor muscle slung underneath like a hammock

find.title: How do you find the muscle?
body: Imagine stopping your urine midstream or holding in wind.
The muscle that lifts in and up at that moment is your pelvic floor.
Repeat that feeling when you're not urinating, lying down or sitting.
find.warn: Don't exercise while urinating. Imagine stopping the flow only once, to find the muscle; doing it repeatedly can stop the bladder from emptying fully.

technique.title: Correct technique
body: Squeeze only the pelvic floor; keep your belly, buttocks and legs relaxed.
Don't hold your breath; keep breathing calmly.
Let the muscle relax fully after every squeeze; relaxing is part of the exercise.
technique.warn: Kegels shouldn't hurt. If you feel pain or discomfort, stop.

trial.title: Practice set 1
trial.body: 3 reps: squeeze for 3 seconds, relax for 3 seconds. Follow the vibration.

check.title: How did set 1 go?
check.body: Could you feel the muscle squeeze and relax?

tips.title: A few tips
body: Try lying down: knees bent, back on the floor. The muscle is easier to feel this way.
Put a hand on your belly; it shouldn't move while you squeeze.
Don't squeeze too hard; a light but clear lift in and up is enough.
It can be hard to feel at first; it gets easier with practice.

position.title: Starting position
body: In the first week you always train in this position.
In later weeks you also train sitting and standing. A card appears when the position changes.

checklist.title: Am I doing it right?
checklist.body: Squeeze once and hold. While holding, go through the list and tick each one you can say “yes” to.

glutes.title: My glutes are relaxed
glutes.text: Your buttock muscles aren't clenching and you aren't lifting up off your seat.

belly.title: My belly is relaxed
belly.text: Put a hand on your belly: it doesn't pull in or harden while you squeeze.

breath.title: I'm still breathing
breath.text: You aren't holding your breath while squeezing; you can breathe in and out easily.

legs.title: My legs are relaxed
legs.text: Your thigh and inner-leg muscles aren't working and you aren't pressing your knees together.

release.title: Practice set 2
release.body: 2 reps: squeeze for 3 seconds, then relax fully for 6 seconds. Let the muscle settle back slowly.

releaseCheck.title: How did set 2 go?
releaseCheck.body: After the squeeze, did you feel the muscle relax fully?

releaseTips.title: Tips for relaxing
body: Don't rush; let the muscle go little by little.
Relax your shoulders and jaw too; tension usually comes together.
Don't bear down as you relax; simply stop holding.

items.title: Holding your breath
items.text: Don't hold your breath while squeezing. Counting out loud helps keep your breath flowing.

items.title: Clenching your glutes
items.text: When your glutes, belly and legs join in, the pelvic floor works less.

items.title: Bearing down
items.text: The muscle draws in and up. Pushing down is the wrong direction; don't bear down when letting go either.

items.title: Too many reps
items.text: More is not always better. A tired muscle works incorrectly; the app sets a daily limit.

ready.title: You're ready!
body: You've found the muscle, learned the vibrations and finished both practice sets.
Your first session is Quick (2 minutes). After that you choose the length; your level adapts to your feedback.

sections.heading: Not medical advice
paragraphs: {{app}} is an educational app for general health and exercise. It is not a medical device; it does not diagnose, treat or prevent any disease.
The information in the app does not replace an examination by, or the advice of, a doctor, urologist or physiotherapist.

sections.heading: Talk to your doctor first
paragraphs: If you have pain in the pelvic area, burning or blood when urinating, a urinary tract infection, prostate problems, recent surgery (especially prostate or pelvic surgery) or a chronic illness, talk to a health professional before you start exercising.
After surgery, your doctor must decide when and how you start exercising.

sections.heading: Stop if you feel pain
paragraphs: If you feel pain, cramps, burning or unexpected discomfort during or after exercise, stop immediately. If the symptoms don't go away, see a health professional.
Overworking the muscles doesn't help. The relaxation phase matters at least as much as the squeeze.

sections.heading: Results vary from person to person
paragraphs: The effect of pelvic floor exercises differs from person to person. {{app}} does not promise any particular improvement or result.
The educational content in the app is for general information, is based on reliable sources and may not yet have had a final expert review.

1.title: Learn the moves
1.text: Do every move slowly and watch the figure; good form matters more than speed.

2.title: Find the rhythm
2.text: Turn 3 sessions a week into a habit; match your breath to the movement.

3.title: Wake up the hips
3.text: Squeeze your glutes on purpose in the bridge and clamshell; pause at the top.

4.title: Strengthen the core
4.text: Keep your back still in dead bug and bird dog; draw your belly in gently.

5.title: More control
5.text: Slow down the lowering; muscle control grows most on the way down.

6.title: Endurance
6.text: Keep your form for the whole session; settle your breath in the rests.

7.title: A lasting habit
7.text: Keep the strength you built; after the programme 2-3 sessions a week are enough.

sources.title: Sources and Method
sources.intro: Every feature in the Smoke-Free Camp is based on research or an official guideline. Here you can see how the camp was built and all the sources it uses.

act.title: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
act.text: The skill lessons and urge surfing teach you to stay with the urge instead of fighting it. In a large randomised trial this approach was linked to higher quit rates than a standard quit-smoking app.

missions.title: Daily missions
missions.text: A short mission every day; each mission is tagged with a behaviour change technique (BCT) code so the content can be checked scientifically.

hsi.title: Level of dependence
hsi.text: The Heaviness of Smoking Index gives a score from 0 to 6 from two questions; it doesn't diagnose, it shows which support will help.

health.title: Health timeline
health.text: Based on the World Health Organization's list of the health benefits of quitting smoking; it varies from person to person.

withdrawal.title: Withdrawal tips
withdrawal.text: Written originally from the US National Cancer Institute and Smokefree.gov guides.

support.title: Professional support
support.text: The app is not a treatment; it points you to free support such as ALO 171, quit-smoking clinics and Yeşilay in Türkiye. It doesn't recommend medicine names or doses.

sources.reviewText: Before publication, the camp's content will be reviewed by a pulmonologist or a certified smoking cessation physician. Right now all content is marked "not yet reviewed".

steps: Squeeze the muscle slowly; reach the top in about 3 seconds.
Hold at the top for half a second.
Let go and wait 1 second, then squeeze slowly again.
intro.note: In Round 2, slow squeezes, quick squeeze-releases and long squeezes come in turn. The phone vibrates while you squeeze and stops when you let go.
intro.demoA11y: Example: the circle grows slowly, pauses briefly at the top and shrinks.
intro.practiceHint: As the circle grows slowly, squeeze slowly too; hold for a moment at the top, then let go fully. The phone vibrates while you squeeze.
checkItems: I squeezed slowly, over about 3 seconds.
I held for a moment at the top, then let go fully.
I didn't hold my breath; my belly and buttocks stayed relaxed.

steps: Squeeze a third: a light lift, 2 seconds.
Squeeze a little more: two thirds, 2 seconds.
On the third step squeeze fully and hold for 2 seconds.
Then let go fully and rest.
checkItems: I felt three separate steps, each a little stronger than the one before.
On the third step I squeezed fully.
I didn't hold my breath; my belly and buttocks stayed relaxed.

steps: Squeeze slowly to full (about 3 seconds) and hold for a moment.
Go down to two thirds: let go a little, but not all the way.
Go down to a third: let go a little more.
Then let go fully.
checkItems: I let go step by step, not all at once.
At each step I could hold that strength for a moment.
At the end I relaxed the muscle fully.

steps: Squeeze fully, 2 seconds.
Let go half way; keep the muscle half squeezed.
Squeeze fully again, 2 seconds.
Then let go fully.
checkItems: Going down to half, I didn't let go fully.
I could squeeze fully a second time.
I didn't hold my breath; my belly and buttocks stayed relaxed.

steps: Squeeze quickly, but only half way.
Let go fully right away.
Half squeeze 1 second, let go 1 second; keep the rhythm.
checkItems: Each squeeze went half way, not fully.
Each time I let go fully.
I kept the rhythm; my belly and buttocks stayed relaxed.

steps: Squeeze half way, not fully.
Hold it there for a long time: don't squeeze harder, don't let go.
When the time is up, let go fully and rest.
checkItems: I held at half strength and didn't squeeze fully.
The strength neither dropped nor rose while I held.
I kept breathing.

steps: Squeeze fully, then let go half way.
Squeeze fully again.
Drop to half and hold it there for a long time.
At the end, let go fully.
checkItems: I could switch between full and half.
I didn't let go during the last half hold.
I didn't hold my breath; my belly and buttocks stayed relaxed.
